DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. An engineer implements a dynamically negotiated LACP port channel on SW1. The port channel members must be configured as active/standby ports with Eth1/2 as active and Eth1/1 as standby. The Eth1/1 interface is configured with default priority. Drag and drop the code snippets from the right onto the blanks in the code on the left to complete the Eth1/2 interface configuration for SW1. Not all code snippets are used.
context: Topology: SW1 connects to SW2 (Eth1/7) and SW3 (Eth1/7) which both connect upstream to a router. SW1's Eth1/1 and Eth1/2 form the port channel toward SW2/SW3.
imageNote: Diagram: SW1 (Eth1/1, Eth1/2) connects up to SW2 (Eth1/7) and SW3 (Eth1/7); SW2 and SW3 both connect up to a router, with SW2-SW3 also directly linked.
theory: When a port channel's lacp max-bundle is set below the number of configured member links, LACP still forms the channel but keeps only the allowed number of links actively forwarding and places the rest in hot-standby; which link wins active status is decided purely by LACP port priority, where a numerically lower value is preferred over a higher one, with any unconfigured member simply using the NX-OS default of 32768. Setting max-bundle to 1 on the port channel is what forces LACP to choose a single active member between the two candidate interfaces based on their relative port-priority values, with the less-preferred link automatically falling back to standby instead of being brought down. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — LACP Max-Bundle and Port Priority for Active/Standby Port Channels)
